open_points.subject: refusal status and detail ownership
open_points.text: the status and the content of every refusal answer;
open_points.question: Does `deliverer_api` own only the construction of refusal responses from `REFUSAL_STATUS` and `REFUSAL_DETAIL`, or does it also own the status and detail values that `data_provider` owns as policy constants?
options: `data_provider` solely owns the status/detail values and `deliverer_api` only applies them
`deliverer_api` owns the values and `data_provider` merely stores them
open_points.default_guess: Treat `data_provider` as the sole owner of the values and `deliverer_api` as the owner only of response construction.

open_points.subject: Authorization extraction and check_token invocation
open_points.text:
The router declares its extractor of the `Authorization` field and names `check_token` as the
resolver of its one principal, but no route it serves calls them: the health route needs no token, and
every route that does is a handler of `deliverer_api`, which reads the field and calls `check_token`
itself, before the project id or the body.
open_points.question: Is the router's declared resolver actually invoked by the generated routing framework, or is it only an unused declaration while each `deliverer_api` handler performs the sole extraction and `check_token` call?
options: The router invokes the resolver and the API handler invokes `check_token` again
Only the API handler extracts the field and invokes `check_token`
The router authenticates and passes the resolved principal to the API handler
open_points.default_guess: Make the router declaration non-executing and have each authenticated API handler perform the single `check_token` call.

witness.initial: The service is running with a valid token and a confirmed project connection, and `check_token` is replaced by a counting test implementation that returns success.
events: The calling flow sends one otherwise valid scan request with exactly one valid `Authorization` field.
The generated router resolves the request and dispatches the `deliverer_api` scan handler.
outcomes: Reading “names `check_token` as the resolver” as executable framework configuration makes the router call `check_token`, after which the handler calls it again.
Reading “no route it serves calls them” literally makes the router dispatch directly and only the handler calls `check_token`.
witness.observer: The integration test observes a count of two calls or one call to `check_token`.
